gaps.sentence: 'You may leave early,' the manager said. The manager said we ___ leave early.
'Don't forget to lock up,' my mother said. My mother reminded me ___ up.
gaps.explanation: 'Don't forget' corresponds to remind + object + to-infinitive.

gaps.sentence: She ___ on seeing the manager immediately.
gaps.explanation: Only 'insist' takes on + -ing; suggest and offer take bare -ing/to-infinitive respectively.

gaps.sentence: 'How much does this cost?' I asked the vendor. I asked the vendor how much it ___.
gaps.explanation: does cost → cost: the past simple of 'cost' is 'cost', used with statement word order.

gaps.sentence: 'The flight leaves now,' the announcer said. The announcer said that the flight left ___.
gaps.explanation: Now becomes then in reported speech.

gaps.sentence: 'Will you marry me?' he asked her. He asked her ___ marry him.
gaps.explanation: Will you...? → if/whether she would...: statement word order, backshifted modal.

gaps.sentence: 'Who broke the window?' the teacher demanded. The teacher demanded ___ the window.
gaps.explanation: 'Demand to know + wh-clause' with statement order; past simple backshifts to past perfect.

gaps.sentence: 'The earth goes round the sun,' the teacher said. The teacher said that the earth ___ round the sun.
gaps.explanation: Timeless general truths may keep the present simple after a past reporting verb.
